steps.intent: Our primary objective is to adapt the obsolete cross-border humanitarian mechanism to realities on the ground, reflecting the Syrian Government's recovered territorial control by closing unnecessary crossings (Al-Ramtha and Al-Yarubiyah) and reducing the authorization period to six months. We expect severe resistance from the Western permanent members and the co-penholders, who insist on maintaining the cross-border mechanism for 12 months and keeping the Al-Yarubiyah crossing open for northeastern Syria without Damascus's consent. Reconciling our insistence on Syrian sovereignty and cross-line aid with their push to preserve unauthorized border access will be the core point of contention.

Delete 'in order to gradually phase out the reliance on cross-border deliveries' and remove language that subordinates cross-border humanitarian assistance to approval by Damascus.

Delete the paragraph or replace it with language reaffirming that cross-border assistance remains an indispensable, non-substitutable humanitarian lifeline to meet the critical needs of civilians across Syria.

messages.Belgium: As humanitarian co-penholder alongside Germany and Kuwait, Belgium cannot support a draft that drastically restricts humanitarian access by excluding vital crossings like Al-Yarubiyah and reducing the mandate to six months. Millions of civilians depend directly on this mechanism for survival, and the United Nations has clearly stated there is no viable alternative to cross-border deliveries. We urge Council members to support the text presented by the humanitarian co-penholders, which strictly reflects operational needs on the ground.
messages.China: China firmly supports the Russian draft resolution, which respects the sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic and properly reflects the evolving realities on the ground. Cross-border humanitarian relief was established as a temporary and exceptional measure and should not substitute for assistance provided through and in coordination with the Syrian Government. We propose a minor technical correction to operational paragraph 1 to resolve the apparent clerical inconsistency regarding the authorized border crossings.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire remains deeply committed to ensuring that vital, life-saving humanitarian assistance reaches all Syrian civilians in need, in full respect of humanitarian principles and international humanitarian law. We believe a 12-month extension provides the necessary predictability for United Nations humanitarian operations, and we urge the penholder to take into full account the operational assessments of humanitarian agencies regarding border crossings. We strongly encourage all delegations to continue constructive consultations to bridge existing divisions and achieve a unified, consensus text.
messages.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic is guided first and foremost by the imperative to ensure unimpeded, life-saving humanitarian assistance to the millions of civilians in dire need across Syria. A six-month renewal and the arbitrary closure of critical border crossings, particularly Al-Yarubiyah in the north-east, would severely jeopardize humanitarian operations in the middle of winter. We urge the penholder to align the draft with the operational recommendations of the Secretary-General and the humanitarian co-penholders.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea attaches the utmost importance to safeguarding the vital flow of humanitarian aid to the Syrian people while upholding the principles of sovereignty and territorial integrity. We urge the Russian delegation and the humanitarian co-penholders to engage in constructive dialogue and show mutual flexibility so that the Council can adopt a compromise resolution by consensus. Avoiding division and political deadlock in the Council must remain our collective priority when civilian lives are at stake.
messages.France: France cannot accept a text that severely curtails the vital cross-border humanitarian mechanism relied upon by millions of Syrian civilians. The arbitrary reduction of the mandate to six months and the removal of critical crossing points, particularly Al-Yarubiyah for the north-east, would have catastrophic humanitarian consequences. We urge Council members to rally behind the balanced humanitarian draft led by Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait.
messages.Germany: As humanitarian co-penholders alongside Belgium and Kuwait, Germany cannot accept a draft that severely weakens the United Nations cross-border mechanism upon which over four million vulnerable Syrian civilians rely. Limiting the renewal to only six months and stripping out vital border crossings—especially Al-Yarubiyah, which provides indispensable medical and humanitarian supplies to northeastern Syria—directly contradicts the explicit assessments and urgent appeals of the Secretary-General and OCHA. Humanitarian access must be determined strictly by humanitarian needs on the ground, not political considerations, and there is currently no viable alternative to cross-border deliveries.
messages.Indonesia: Indonesia consistently emphasizes that the Security Council must put the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people first and act in unity to save lives. We are deeply concerned that reducing border crossings and shortening the renewal period to six months will severely hinder the United Nations' ability to deliver critical aid to millions in dire need. We urge the delegation of the Russian Federation to engage constructively with the co-penholders (Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait) to find a consensus text that preserves vital humanitarian lifelines.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait, as co-penholder on the Syrian humanitarian dossier alongside Belgium and Germany, cannot support a draft that drastically scales back the United Nations cross-border humanitarian mechanism against the clear assessments of the Secretary-General and humanitarian actors. Reducing the mandate to six months and cutting vital border crossings, particularly Al-Yarubiyah and Bab al-Salam, will directly jeopardize the delivery of life-saving aid to millions of civilians in desperate need as winter sets in. We urge the penholder to preserve a 12-month renewal and maintain the necessary crossings so the Council can respond meaningfully to the dire humanitarian realities on the ground.
messages.Peru: Peru attaches the highest priority to alleviating the suffering of the Syrian people and ensuring the uninterrupted delivery of life-saving humanitarian aid, in full alignment with the United Nations assessment and the efforts of the humanitarian co-penholders (Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait). We believe that curtailing the duration to six months and cutting vital access points, particularly for the north-east, jeopardizes critical humanitarian operations on the ground. We urge the penholder to align the text with the Secretary-General's recommendations so the Council can preserve a principled, effective humanitarian response.
messages.Poland: Poland cannot accept the draft resolution in its current form, as it drastically scales down the cross-border humanitarian mechanism at a time of severe and mounting civilian suffering. Arbitrarily reducing the mandate duration to six months and cutting crucial border crossings, particularly Al-Yarubiyah, directly contradicts the explicit assessments and urgent requests of the Secretary-General and OCHA. Poland fully supports the approach of the humanitarian co-penholders (Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait) and urges the Council to preserve a 12-month mandate with sufficient border crossings to ensure life-saving aid reaches all Syrians in need.
messages.South Africa: South Africa firmly believes that the acute suffering of innocent Syrian civilians must remain the Council's paramount consideration and must not be politicized. While we appreciate the penholder's initiative to maintain the cross-border lifeline, extending the mandate for twelve months is vital to provide operational certainty and predictability for United Nations humanitarian agencies on the ground. We urge all delegations to show flexibility and bridge divides so that vital humanitarian assistance reaches all those in need without interruption.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot accept this draft resolution, which seeks to gut a vital humanitarian lifeline that millions of vulnerable Syrian civilians depend upon for survival. Arbitrarily reducing the mandate to six months and cutting essential crossings—notably Al-Yarubiyah, which delivers critical medical supplies to the northeast—is completely unacceptable and detached from humanitarian realities. We urge Council members instead to support the balanced 12-month renewal prepared by the humanitarian co-penholders.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot accept a text that guts life-saving humanitarian access by arbitrarily eliminating critical border crossings—most urgently Al-Yarubiyah in the north-east—and reducing the mandate to an unworkable six months. Over four million Syrians depend on the UN cross-border mechanism, and cross-line aid through Damascus cannot substitute for this indispensable lifeline. We urge Council members to support the compromise text put forward by the humanitarian co-penholders rather than politicizing emergency assistance to the Syrian people.

steps.summary: The Russian Federation corrected the clerical error in OP1 to clearly authorize solely Bab al-Hawa and Bab al-Salam for a period of six months, firmly rejecting the inclusion of Al-Yarubiyah and Al-Ramtha. In response to constructive suggestions from African and Latin American delegations, PP4, OP3, and OP4 were refined to emphasize United Nations humanitarian principles, cross-line and cross-border complementarity, and reporting on alternative delivery modalities, while maintaining core Russian principles on Syrian sovereignty and preventing aid diversion to terrorists.

messages.Belgium: As co-penholder on the humanitarian file in Syria, Belgium cannot accept a draft that excludes the Al-Yarubiyah crossing and slashes the mandate duration to six months in the middle of winter. The cross-border mechanism remains an indispensable lifeline, and there is currently no viable cross-line alternative to supply vital medical and relief items to the millions of civilians in north-east Syria. Unless the draft preserves three border crossings and provides a 12-month extension to ensure operational certainty, Belgium will not support it.
messages.China: China appreciates the penholder's efforts and fully supports the revised draft resolution. The text appropriately reflects the evolving situation on the ground in Syria, respects the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, and adheres to the guiding principles of United Nations humanitarian assistance in accordance with General Assembly resolution 46/182. China stands ready to vote in favour of this draft resolution.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire welcomes the penholder’s constructive revisions in PP4 and OP3 emphasizing United Nations humanitarian principles and the primary objective of delivering relief to populations in need. While we maintain that a twelve-month renewal offers necessary operational predictability for humanitarian partners, our overriding objective is to ensure that life-saving cross-border aid is not interrupted. We call on all Council members to bridge their differences through dialogue so as to preserve Council unity and safeguard aid delivery to the Syrian people.
messages.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic remains guided strictly by the humanitarian imperative and the documented needs of millions of civilians relying on United Nations cross-border assistance. In line with the clear assessment of the Secretary-General and humanitarian partners, reauthorizing the Al-Yarubiyah crossing and ensuring a 12-month mandate are critical to avoid catastrophic gaps in life-saving aid, especially in north-east Syria. Since these essential requirements have not been incorporated, our delegation cannot support the text in its current form and will abstain.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea welcomes the penholder's efforts to clarify the text and reflect the essential complementarity between cross-border and cross-line deliveries. Our primary concern remains ensuring that millions of Syrian civilians continue to receive vital humanitarian aid without disruption, while upholding Syrian sovereignty and Council unity. We strongly encourage the penholder and the humanitarian co-penholders to show reciprocal flexibility on duration and crossings so that this Council can speak with one voice on this purely humanitarian matter.
messages.France: France cannot accept a draft that arbitrarily restricts life-saving humanitarian assistance by cutting the mandate to six months and eliminating critical border crossings, notably Al-Yarubiyah, which is indispensable for providing medical aid to northeastern Syria. Humanitarian aid must respond to needs on the ground as documented by the Secretary-General, not to political agendas, and cross-line deliveries cannot currently replace the cross-border mechanism. Unless these essential crossings and a twelve-month duration are restored, France will vote against this text.
messages.Germany: As humanitarian co-penholder alongside Belgium and Kuwait, Germany cannot support a draft resolution that deprives over a million vulnerable civilians in north-east Syria of critical medical and humanitarian relief by closing the Al-Yarubiyah crossing. Furthermore, a 12-month renewal is indispensable to ensure operational predictability and continuity for humanitarian agencies on the ground. In the absence of these essential provisions, Germany will vote against this text.
messages.Indonesia: Indonesia thanks the Russian delegation for accommodating our proposed language on OP 3 regarding complementarity. However, in line with the clear assessments provided by UN humanitarian agencies, a twelve-month renewal and sufficient cross-border access remain essential to provide operational predictability and alleviate civilian suffering. Indonesia reiterates that Council unity must be prioritized to put people first, and without bridging these core humanitarian requirements, my delegation will be unable to support the draft and will be obliged to abstain.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait regrets that the humanitarian imperatives underscored by the Secretary-General and OCHA—specifically a 12-month renewal and the preservation of Al-Yarubiyah to assist over a million people in the northeast—have been disregarded. A six-month mandate creates severe operational instability for humanitarian agencies in the dead of winter. Unless these vital humanitarian lifelines are preserved, Kuwait cannot support the draft in its current form.
messages.Peru: Peru appreciates the penholder's consideration of humanitarian principles in the text, but we remain deeply concerned that the draft limits the renewal to only six months and excludes the Al-Yarubiyah crossing. According to United Nations humanitarian assessments, Al-Yarubiyah is essential for delivering vital medical supplies and assistance to civilians in north-east Syria, and operational predictability requires a 12-month mandate. In the absence of these critical elements necessary to meet urgent humanitarian needs, Peru cannot support the draft text in its current form.
messages.Poland: Poland cannot support a draft that severely weakens the United Nations humanitarian response by eliminating the Al-Yarubiyah crossing and reducing the mandate to only six months. At a time when millions of civilians depend on cross-border aid for their survival, cutting off established lifelines and creating operational uncertainty is unacceptable. Ensuring unhindered, predictable, and principled humanitarian access is our collective legal and moral obligation, and we cannot vote in favour of this text in its current form.
messages.South Africa: South Africa appreciates the incorporation of United Nations humanitarian principles in operative paragraph 3. We reiterate that a twelve-month renewal is vital to give humanitarian agencies the predictability and operational stability required to assist civilians in dire need. South Africa remains committed to ensuring that life-saving humanitarian access is not disrupted and urges all Council members to bridge divides so that innocent lives are placed above political considerations.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support a draft resolution that deliberately compromises the United Nations humanitarian response by halving the mandate to six months and cutting off the Al-Yarubiyah crossing, which delivers essential medical supplies and relief to over one million people in north-east Syria. The Council has a clear responsibility to heed the warnings of the Secretary-General and humanitarian agencies, who have repeatedly underscored that there is no viable alternative to cross-border aid. As the penholder refuses to accommodate these vital humanitarian requirements, the United Kingdom will vote against this draft.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot accept a text that guts life-saving cross-border aid by removing the Al-Yarubiyah crossing and slashing the mandate duration to six months. Stripping access to north-east Syria will directly deprive over a million civilians of desperately needed medical supplies and humanitarian relief, with no viable cross-line alternative available. Unless the text authorizes the three essential crossings for twelve months, the United States will vote against this draft.

steps.summary: The Russian Federation maintains the draft resolution without alterations, reaffirming its principled position that the cross-border humanitarian mechanism is an extraordinary and temporary measure that must reflect the evolving territorial realities in Syria. Requests from Western delegations to reinsert the Al-Yarubiyah crossing and extend the mandate to twelve months are firmly rejected as infringements on Syrian sovereignty, while the draft ensures the continued flow of aid through two north-western crossings for six months alongside strict measures against terrorist diversion.

vetoed_by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

reasons.Belgium: As co-penholder of the humanitarian file on Syria alongside Germany and Kuwait, Belgium opposes the Russian draft resolution because it arbitrarily cuts vital cross-border access points—particularly Al-Yarubiyah, which provides critical medical aid to north-eastern Syria—and halves the mandate to six months, failing to meet the minimum requirements outlined by the UN humanitarian agencies.
reasons.China: China consistently supports respect for Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity, recognizing that the situation on the ground has evolved and that the cross-border mechanism should be adjusted accordingly. China supports the Russian draft resolution to renew authorization for two border crossings for six months and will deliver its statement explaining its vote after the voting concludes.
reasons.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire supports maintaining the vital cross-border humanitarian mechanism to ensure uninterrupted aid delivery to millions of Syrian civilians in need, even under a reduced six-month authorization and fewer crossings, rather than seeing the mandate expire entirely.
reasons.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic abstains because our core concern—ensuring predictable, comprehensive 12-month humanitarian access including the Al-Yarubiyah crossing for vulnerable populations in north-east Syria—was rejected by the penholder. We maintain our principled stance supporting humanitarian needs while avoiding further division in the Council.
reasons.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supports extending the cross-border humanitarian mechanism to ensure vital assistance continues to reach vulnerable Syrian populations, aligning with the African members (A3) to preserve humanitarian access while urging council unity.
reasons.France: France opposes the Russian draft resolution because it severely curtails the cross-border humanitarian mechanism by eliminating the Al-Yarubiyah crossing and reducing the mandate to only six months, which endangers millions of civilians dependent on cross-border aid in northern Syria.
reasons.Germany: As co-penholder for the Syrian humanitarian file alongside Belgium and Kuwait, Germany cannot support a draft resolution that halves the authorization period to six months and eliminates the critical Al-Yarubiyah crossing in the north-east, which leaves millions of civilians without vital, irreplaceable humanitarian assistance in defiance of the Secretary-General's assessments.
reasons.Indonesia: Indonesia abstained on the draft resolution because, while recognizing the vital need to maintain cross-border humanitarian access, the proposed text reduced crucial crossing points and the mandate's duration contrary to United Nations humanitarian assessments and without council-wide consensus.
reasons.Kuwait: As a co-penholder of the humanitarian cross-border file alongside Belgium and Germany, Kuwait cannot support the Russian draft resolution, which reduces the authorized border crossings and duration against the clear recommendations of the Secretary-General and humanitarian agencies; however, in line with our position and consultation with partners, Kuwait abstains on this draft.
reasons.Peru: Peru abstains because the draft resolution significantly curtails vital cross-border humanitarian operations by reducing authorized crossings and shortening the authorization period to six months, failing to incorporate our key priorities while falling short of the humanitarian needs identified by the United Nations.
reasons.Poland: The Russian draft resolution severely weakens the United Nations cross-border humanitarian mechanism by cutting vital border crossings and halving the mandate's duration to six months, failing to meet critical humanitarian needs and ignoring our red lines; Poland therefore votes against it in alignment with our EU and Western partners.
reasons.Russian Federation: As the sponsor of this draft resolution, the Russian Federation strongly supports its own text, which reflects our long-standing position that the cross-border mechanism must be adapted to changed realities on the ground, respect Syrian sovereignty, and phase out redundant border crossings.
reasons.South Africa: South Africa votes in favour because maintaining the cross-border humanitarian mechanism, even in a reduced form of two border crossings for six months, is vital to prevent the complete collapse of life-saving aid deliveries to millions of civilians in need.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The Russian draft resolution severely weakens the UN's cross-border humanitarian mechanism by stripping the Al-Yarubiyah crossing in the north-east and halving the mandate's duration to six months, which directly undermines vital aid delivery to millions of vulnerable civilians. In line with our established foreign policy and our red lines, the United Kingdom votes against this inadequate text.
reasons.United States of America: The United States opposes Russia's draft resolution because it drastically reduces the cross-border mechanism to only two crossings, removes the vital Al-Yarubiyah crossing serving north-east Syria, and cuts the authorization period to six months, directly undermining life-saving humanitarian assistance.

before.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation has submitted this draft resolution because we believe that the Security Council must act responsibly and take into account the reality on the ground in Syria. 

Resolution 2165 (2014) was adopted as an urgent, extraordinary and temporary mechanism at a time when the Syrian Government lacked control over vast parts of its territory and when there were no other means to deliver aid. Today, the situation has changed radically. The Syrian Government has regained control over most of its territory, and cross-line deliveries can and must be expanded in full respect of the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, in accordance with the guiding principles of humanitarian assistance set out in General Assembly resolution 46/182.

There is no justification for maintaining the Al-Ramtha crossing point on the Jordanian border, which has not been used for over a year and a half, nor the Al-Yarubiyah crossing on the border with Iraq, where the situation on the ground has evolved significantly and assistance can be delivered from within Syria. 

Our draft resolution takes a pragmatic approach: it maintains the cross-border mechanism through the two active border crossings in Turkey—Bab al-Hawa and Bab al-Salam—for six months, thereby ensuring that humanitarian assistance continues to reach those in genuine need in north-western Syria without disruption, while preventing aid from falling into the hands of terrorists. 

This is the only realistic, compromise text on the table. Those who vote against it will demonstrate that their concern is not the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people, but rather the preservation of an outdated mechanism for political motives. We urge all members of the Council to support our draft resolution.
before.United States of America:
The United States will vote against this draft resolution. Today, Russia and China vetoed a principled, compromise text authored by Germany, Belgium, and Kuwait that would have sustained life-saving cross-border humanitarian assistance for four million Syrians in desperate need. Having just blocked critical relief, Russia now presents a draft text that is nothing more than a cynical political maneuver designed to choke off cross-border aid, severing the Yarubiyah crossing in the north-east and cutting the mandate down to six months. 

There is no viable alternative to cross-border delivery to meet the sheer scale of humanitarian suffering caused by the Assad regime's continued atrocities against its own people. Gutting this lifeline and dismantling crossings upon which millions depend for food, medicine, and shelter is unconscionable. The United States will not be complicit in this effort to abandon vulnerable civilians, and we urge all Council members to vote against this draft resolution.

after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation, and we regret that it was not adopted.

China has always attached great importance to the humanitarian situation in Syria and has consistently provided humanitarian assistance to the Syrian people to the best of its ability through both bilateral and multilateral channels. At the same time, China has always maintained that the provision of humanitarian assistance to Syria must strictly adhere to the United Nations guiding principles for humanitarian emergency assistance set out in General Assembly resolution 46/182, and must fully respect the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. The views and sovereignty of the Syrian Government should be respected, and humanitarian operations must be coordinated closely with it.

The cross-border humanitarian mechanism established pursuant to resolution 2165 (2014) was a temporary and extraordinary arrangement adopted under specific historical circumstances. In the light of the significant developments and changes on the ground in Syria, the Council should objectively assess the situation and make appropriate and realistic adjustments to the mechanism, while vigorously promoting cross-line operations to deliver humanitarian aid.

The Russian draft resolution took into full consideration the evolving realities on the ground, addressed the urgent need to maintain the flow of humanitarian assistance to the Syrian people, and sought to preserve the cross-border mechanism with reasonable adjustments to the number of border crossings and the mandate’s duration. It was a constructive effort to bridge differences and avoid a vacuum in the provision of humanitarian assistance. Based on this consistent position, China voted in favour of the draft resolution.

China also firmly rejects the unfounded accusations and attacks made earlier by certain Council members against China’s voting position. China decides its vote independently based on the merits of the matter itself. We believe that politicizing humanitarian issues and imposing unilateral coercive measures against Syria have severely compounded the economic difficulties and humanitarian suffering of the Syrian people. We call on all parties to eliminate unilateral sanctions, step up counter-terrorism efforts, and continue consultations to find an appropriate solution that genuinely serves the interests of the Syrian people.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Dominican Republic:
The Dominican Republic deeply regrets that the Security Council was unable to reach consensus today on a matter of vital humanitarian importance for millions of Syrian civilians.

We voted in favour of the draft resolution presented by Belgium, Germany and Kuwait, and we commend the co-penholders for their tireless and transparent efforts to bridge differences and preserve unity within the Council. The cross-border mechanism authorized by resolution 2165 (2014) is not a political tool; it is a vital lifeline upon which more than 4 million people depend for their survival, including millions of women and children, particularly as winter sets in and humanitarian conditions on the ground continue to deteriorate.

The Dominican Republic abstained on the draft resolution presented by the Russian Federation. While we recognize the importance of sovereignty and the ultimate objective of expanding cross-line operations throughout the Syrian territory, the reality today is that there is no viable alternative to the cross-border mechanism to meet the immense scale of humanitarian needs in northern Syria. Reducing the number of authorized border crossings and curtailing the mandate to six months would drastically undermine the capacity of the United Nations and its humanitarian partners to deliver predictable, timely and effective life-saving assistance to populations in desperate need.

Humanitarian assistance must be guided strictly by the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence, and it must never be held hostage to political considerations. The failure to adopt a resolution today sends a devastating message to the millions of Syrians who rely on the United Nations for food, medicine and shelter.

With the current mandate set to expire on 10 January, we urge all members of the Council to put the lives and well-being of the Syrian people above all other interests. We call for renewed, constructive engagement to find a solution that guarantees the uninterrupted delivery of humanitarian aid to those who need it most.
after.France:
France deeply regrets the veto cast today by Russia and China on the draft resolution presented by Belgium, Germany and Kuwait, which was a balanced, responsible and strictly humanitarian text. That draft resolution was the result of weeks of tireless negotiations by the co-penholders to preserve a vital humanitarian lifeline for four million Syrians.

France voted against the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. We did so because that text does not meet the immense humanitarian needs on the ground. The Russian proposal would arbitrarily eliminate the Al-Yarubiyah border crossing, which is essential for providing medical supplies and humanitarian assistance to 1.4 million people in north-eastern Syria, where there is currently no viable alternative. Furthermore, reducing the mandate to six months would only create deep uncertainty for humanitarian actors and disrupt operations in the midst of winter. 

Let us be clear: cross-line assistance, which we support in principle, cannot replace the cross-border mechanism. The Syrian regime has consistently instrumentalized humanitarian aid, denying access to populations in need and using starvation as a weapon of war. There is no alternative today to the cross-border mechanism authorized by resolution 2165 (2014) to deliver assistance directly, impartially and efficiently to populations outside the regime’s control.

The humanitarian situation in Syria, particularly in Idlib, is catastrophic and deteriorating rapidly under the relentless bombing campaign conducted by the regime and its allies against civilians and civilian infrastructure, including hospitals and schools, in flagrant violation of international humanitarian law.

The mandate of resolution 2449 (2018) expires on 10 January 2020. It is our collective and moral duty to find a solution before that date to preserve cross-border humanitarian aid for the millions of Syrian civilians who depend on it for their survival. France remains fully committed to working with all Council members to achieve that vital objective.
after.Germany:
I speak in my national capacity to explain Germany’s vote against the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation.

Today is a dark day for the Syrian people and a dark day for the Security Council. Just moments ago, draft resolution S/2019/961, carefully crafted by the humanitarian co-penholders—Belgium, Kuwait and Germany—and supported by 13 members of this Council, was vetoed. That text was a thoroughly negotiated, balanced and principled humanitarian compromise based on the clear, evidence-based assessment and urgent appeal of the Secretary-General and the United Nations humanitarian agencies.

The draft resolution just presented by the Russian Federation does not meet the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people. It falls far short of what is required to keep millions of innocent civilians alive. 

First, by eliminating the Al-Yarubiyah crossing in the north-east, this draft text would effectively sever a vital humanitarian lifeline for 1.4 million people in need, including hundreds of thousands of displaced persons. The Secretary-General has repeatedly made clear that cross-line deliveries cannot replace the scale and scope of cross-border operations, particularly for urgently needed medical supplies. We cannot accept arbitrarily cutting off life-saving assistance to populations that have no viable alternative.

Second, reducing the renewal period from twelve months to just six months undermines the operational predictability, stability and planning that United Nations agencies and humanitarian non-governmental organizations desperately need to organize complex logistics in extremely challenging conditions. 

Humanitarian aid must never be politicized, instrumentalized or used as leverage. The mandate established by resolution 2165 (2014) is not a political tool; it is a vital mechanism designed to save human lives when all other options fail. Germany could not and will not support a text that hollows out this essential humanitarian mechanism and leaves millions of vulnerable Syrians without adequate support.

The current mandate under resolution 2449 (2018) runs until 10 January 2020. Germany, together with our co-penholders, will not give up on the Syrian people. We will work tirelessly in the coming days and weeks to ensure that the Council fulfills its humanitarian duty and maintains this indispensable cross-border mechanism.
after.Kuwait:
At the outset, I would like to express our deep regret and disappointment at the Council’s failure today to adopt draft resolution S/2019/961, submitted by the humanitarian co-penholders — Belgium, Germany, and my country, Kuwait — to renew the cross-border humanitarian aid mechanism in Syria. 

Over the past weeks, as co-penholders, we have worked tirelessly, transparently, and in good faith to reach a compromise that addresses the concerns of all Council members while preserving the vital, life-saving nature of the cross-border mechanism. We listened to all delegations and made substantial concessions, including reducing the number of border crossings from four to three. Our sole objective throughout this process has been purely humanitarian: to ensure that critical, life-saving aid continues to reach over 4 million Syrians in need, who rely on cross-border assistance for their survival, particularly with the onset of harsh winter conditions.

Cross-border assistance remains an indispensable lifeline. As the Secretary-General and the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs have repeatedly made clear, there is currently no viable alternative to the cross-border mechanism to meet the massive humanitarian needs in northern Syria. Cross-line deliveries, while important and encouraged, cannot at this stage substitute for the scale and scope of cross-border operations.

With regard to the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation (S/2019/962), Kuwait decided to abstain. We believe that the draft does not adequately respond to the humanitarian needs assessed by the United Nations on the ground, as it reduces the duration of the mandate to only six months and removes the Al-Yarubiyah crossing, which serves over one million people in north-eastern Syria who have no other reliable means of receiving critical medical supplies. However, out of our steadfast commitment to the humanitarian cause and our belief that preserving any avenue of aid to the Syrian people is essential, Kuwait could not cast a negative vote against a text that sought to renew the mechanism, even in a limited form. For Kuwait, the humanitarian imperative must always take precedence over political considerations.

The mandate of resolution 2449 (2018) does not expire until 10 January 2020. As Kuwait approaches the end of its tenure as an elected member of this Council, we appeal to all members of the Security Council to set aside political differences and redouble their efforts in the coming days to reach a consensus that ensures the continuation of cross-border humanitarian deliveries. The Syrian people are looking to this Council, and we must not fail them.

Finally, we reiterate our firm stance that there is no military solution to the Syrian crisis. The only viable path to ending the suffering of the Syrian people is through an inclusive, Syrian-led political process in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015) and the 2012 Geneva Communiqué, preserving the unity, sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of Syria.
after.Russian Federation:
(spoke in Russian):

I would like to ask those Council members who just voted against our draft resolution: who won today? 

Nobody won. Only the Syrian people lost. 

Today, you had the opportunity to adopt a viable compromise decision that would have extended the cross-border mechanism for six months through the two border crossings that are actually in demand and operational, while fully taking into account the realities on the ground. 

Instead, our Western colleagues preferred political games, demagogy, and geopolitical ambitions over the real needs of the Syrian people. You rejected our draft simply because it was submitted by the Russian Federation and because it did not satisfy your desire to preserve an obsolete mechanism that infringes on the sovereignty of the Syrian Arab Republic and serves to sustain terrorist enclaves in Idlib. 

Do not try to shift the blame onto Russia. The responsibility for the fact that the Security Council was unable today to adopt a decision extending cross-border humanitarian assistance lies squarely on those who voted against our draft resolution.
after.South Africa:
Mr. President,

South Africa voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation, just as we voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted earlier by the co-penholders, Belgium, Germany and Kuwait. 

South Africa’s consistent position has always been that the primary and urgent focus of the Security Council must be on addressing the dire humanitarian situation of the Syrian people. Millions of innocent civilians, particularly vulnerable groups such as women, children and the elderly, depend on the life-saving assistance provided through the United Nations cross-border mechanism, especially as the harsh winter sets in.

We are deeply disappointed that the Security Council was unable to reach consensus today on this critical matter. The humanitarian needs of the Syrian people should never be politicized, nor should life-saving aid be held hostage to geopolitical considerations. Council members must overcome their divisions and prioritize the suffering of innocent human beings.

South Africa firmly upholds the principles of the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations. We also recognize that while cross-line delivery should be expanded and enhanced wherever possible in coordination with the Syrian authorities, the reality on the ground makes cross-border delivery an indispensable lifeline that cannot be abruptly severed without catastrophic humanitarian consequences.

It is for these reasons that South Africa supported both texts, with the overriding objective of ensuring that the mechanism for providing humanitarian assistance is renewed and that aid continues to reach all those in need without disruption.

We strongly urge all members of the Council to put aside their differences and to use the time remaining before the expiration of the current mandate to engage constructively and in a spirit of compromise, in order to ensure that an agreement is reached that safeguards the continuous delivery of humanitarian assistance to the people of Syria.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
I thank the humanitarian co-penholders—Belgium, Germany and Kuwait—for their tireless efforts over recent weeks to craft a balanced, compromise text that put the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people first. 

The United Kingdom is appalled by the decision of the Russian Federation and China earlier today to veto the co-penholders’ draft resolution. In doing so, they have blocked the delivery of vital, life-saving aid to millions of vulnerable civilians who face a catastrophic humanitarian situation, exacerbated by the relentless and indiscriminate bombardment of Idlib by the Syrian regime and its Russian allies.

The draft resolution just put forward by the Russian Federation was never a serious attempt to address humanitarian needs. Instead, it was an unacceptable political attempt to dismantle a mechanism that the United Nations itself has repeatedly described as irreplaceable. By stripping out the Al-Yarubiyah crossing in the north-east, Russia’s text sought to arbitrarily cut off over 1.4 million civilians from critical medical supplies and assistance that cannot be delivered across conflict lines. Furthermore, reducing the mandate to six months would have plunged humanitarian operations into uncertainty in the middle of winter, creating unnecessary logistical chaos for aid workers on the ground.

Cross-border assistance is not a political choice; it is an absolute humanitarian imperative. There is currently no viable alternative to cross-border delivery to reach millions of Syrians in need, precisely because the Syrian regime systematically weaponizes aid, refuses access and starves its own people.

The United Kingdom voted against this Russian draft resolution because we refuse to endorse a cynical maneuver that would compromise the fundamental principles of humanitarian assistance and abandon vulnerable civilians. We urge all Council members to come together before the mandate expires to find a way forward that genuinely protects and supports the Syrian people.
